text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Shares from the mass sell-off programme are being traded outside the OTC market and the Bucharest stock exchange, Stefan Boboc, head of the National Securities Commission, told a parliament panel.

- The Transport Ministry blocked 124 investment projects due to funds shortages, minister Traian Basescu said. He said Romania would invest in four objectives, including national road and rail networks, the Bucharest subway and the international Otopeni airport.
- Romania recovered only some 10 percent of sums from fiscal evasion cases revealed by police in 1996.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian Oil Company (CRP) has some 100,000 tonnes of diesel in stock for the spring farming campaign, but only some 7,000 tonnes were sold in March. The CRP will export the diesel surplus.
- Parliament's finance commissions want the health budget to be at least 4.0 percent of GDP, saying it can be funded from the 10 percent originally provided for social protection.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Italy ranks second among Romania's trade partners. Trade exchanges rose 2.5 times in the past two years.
- Commercial banks can grant up to 550 billion lei in farming credits for the spring campaign.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania will invest 172 billion lei in 1997 to upgrade and extend its main international airport Otopeni.
All newspapers report on the summit between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The former leftist ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) whose MPs walked out of parliament on Monday, will vote for the 1997 draft state budget during debates in parliament.
- Emilio Gabaglio, secretary of the European Trade Union Confederation said Romania has "all chances to join the European Union".
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes a report by the Court of Accounts on the 1995 budget of the capital city of Bucharest.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The PDSR will end parliament walkout said its leader Ion Iliescu after talks with President Emil Constantinescu.
- Romania's army has problems linked with its equipment and capacity to ensure decent conditions to soldiers and officers, said Constantinescu after meeting senior defence officials.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc said $1.5 billion over the next seven to eight years would solve the problems of the Romanian army.
JURNALUL NATIONAL

- "Romania does not want to be left in a grey or dark zone after the Helsinki summit" reads newspaper's headline to column on leading politicians' opinions on the Helsinki summit. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
